# LumiSynth notices

This Tide source tree incorporates LumiSynth from [chthollyphile/lumisynth](https://github.com/chthollyphile/lumisynth), upstream commit `a936c4e866387088b13ca819358d307d269be799`. The incorporated source is licensed under **GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only (AGPL-3.0-only)**; see `LICENSE`. The source currently resides in `vendor/lumisynth/src/` in this Tide checkout. This notice does not claim that this checkout or its source is already publicly available.

Tide's integration changes are listed in `manifest.json`. The original sonnet, tempera, lumiere, and hanabi packs and their rendering algorithms are retained. Their optional React settings-panel registrations are removed from the embedded runtime entry; Sonnet's React-based Lucide icon-to-texture path remains and its exact dependencies are listed in the manifest. Tide drives the original Pixi kernel using its audio clock, disables its independent ticker, and loads the local stage bundle only when a stage is selected. The bundle externalizes LumiSynth's optional `mediabunny` exact-video export dependency; that export path is not provided by Tide's stage integration.

Tide's existing program is licensed under `GPL-3.0-only`. AGPLv3 section 13 permits combining an AGPLv3-covered work with a GPLv3 work in one combined work, while applying the corresponding terms to the covered components and the combination. Distribution of Tide with this stage must satisfy the applicable AGPL and GPL source, license, modification-notice, and user-notice requirements. In particular, if a distributed or operated version supports remote network interaction with users, section 13 requires a prominent opportunity for those users to obtain the Corresponding Source of that version. The stage source, build inputs, and source changes are present in this checkout; any release must provide the Corresponding Source for the exact distributed version through an accessible source archive or repository revision. The desktop release has not been published as part of this integration work.

The build places the LumiSynth license, this notice, the manifest, and the React/ReactDOM/Lucide third-party notices under `dist/licenses/lumisynth/`. These notices do not replace or modify any upstream license text or copyright notice.
